about: What this repo can distribute as a bank, and what it never distributes. This file is the source of truth, superseding the prose inventory in issue #219 — that one drifted from the repo and shipped wrong paths. It records the two things that cannot be derived. `bundles` are named groups of content that cannot be a package, because the tools that read it require it at a fixed repo-relative path. `exclude` records the paths deliberately left out and why. The bank's *package* set is not listed here: it is every workspace package the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` globs match, minus anything under `exclude`, so a package that is added, moved or renamed needs no edit (ADR 0039). A consumer's bank.manifest.json names packages and bundles; `bank:sync` resolves that selection to the transitive workspace closure of paths at the pinned ref, and reads nothing else. Paths here are prefixes — bank:sync has no per-path exclusion, so anything on `exclude` must be a path that no selectable prefix already covers. `scripts/check-bank-paths.mjs` fails `pnpm lint` when a tracked root-level entry is in neither a bundle nor `exclude`.

bundles.name: root
bundles.description: The workspace itself: what pnpm, turbo, the hooks and the gate read from a fixed repo-relative path. Required by every selection, so it is never a choice. `patches/` travels with pnpm-workspace.yaml because the workspace file carries a patchedDependencies entry pointing into it — sync one without the other and `pnpm install` fails outright. `scripts/` is here rather than split per concern because the root package.json's script entries all point into it, including the infra scripts the `infra` bundle depends on. package.json travels with `scripts/` for the same reason read the other way: the script entries are the only thing that invokes those files, and the ten root devDependencies they run on (turbo, prettier, lefthook, knip, syncpack, tsx, typescript, @turbo/gen, dotenv-cli, jsdom) are declared nowhere else. Only `name` in it is consumer identity, and a field the bank never edits and the consumer sets once conflicts exactly never under three-way merge — the seed model `packages/platform/env` and tailwind's theme.css already use. A consumer that arrives with its own manifest omits it (docs/bank.md).

bundles.name: scaffolding
bundles.description: The generator behind `turbo gen`, so a consumer can scaffold the packages it is creating with the same templates Trellis uses. It never touches packages taken from the bank — those arrive through bank:sync.

bundles.name: agents
bundles.description: Agent configuration, so a harness arrives already knowing the repo rather than being reconstructed. `.agents/skills/` is the one agent-agnostic source; AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md are the per-harness entry points onto it; skills-lock.json pins each skill to its upstream by content hash; .claudeignore is the committed source that scripts/sync-claudeignore.mjs compiles into deny rules, and .claude/settings.json is where those rules land alongside the authored permissions.allow, the disable* flags and the bootstrap hook — sync-claudeignore.mjs writes one of its keys, a human wrote the rest, and nothing else in this bundle carries them. scripts/register-skills.sh is named explicitly even though `scripts/` already covers it, so the bundle reads as self-sufficient.

bundles.name: ci
bundles.description: The workflows, the composite setup action every job calls, and the dependency-update configuration. These live under `.github/` rather than in a tooling package because GitHub only loads workflows from that fixed repo-relative path — the reason this is a bundle and not a package. `.github/actions/setup` is the one path-flexible piece (`uses:` takes any repo path) and is kept beside the workflows that are its only consumer. Named as three paths rather than `.github/` wholesale so the directory splits by concern: the only other thing in it is copilot-instructions.md, a per-harness entry point belonging to the `agents` bundle.

bundles.name: docs
bundles.description: The repo-wide ADRs and the agent protocol docs, which AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md link into by relative path, so taking the agents bundle without this one leaves those links dangling. Package-scoped reasoning is not here: it travels with the package, in its own docs/adr.

bundles.name: infra
bundles.description: The local dev stack: the compose file plus the assets it mounts. Selected automatically when any selected package declares `acme.infra` in its package.json — derived from the graph, never a hardcoded list (scripts/resolve-infra.ts is the same convention). The scripts that drive it (compose.sh, infra.sh, infra-up.sh, resolve-compose-env.ts, resolve-infra.ts) come from the always-included `root` bundle, so `pnpm infra:up` always finds the compose file its `-f deploy/compose.yaml` names.

exclude.reason: Repository identity — a consumer's front page is never ours.
Repository identity — the consumer's licensing is its own decision.
An index of this repo's packages. A consumer takes a subset, so ours would be wrong on arrival; each package's own CONTEXT.md travels with it.

Its header says committed and non-secret, which is true and misleading: it maps secret names to each app's env file. A consumer rewrites the mapping wholesale while Trellis edits the same lines whenever it adds an app.
Resolved from the consumer's own manifest set. Syncing ours would pin packages it does not have.

An app is the consumer's own. The bank distributes packages and configuration and never an app — `pnpm prune <app>` is the separate path for starting from a Trellis app, and #240 puts producing a runnable application out of scope.

Symlinks, generated by scripts/register-skills.sh on postinstall from .agents/skills/. Vendoring them ships links a consumer has to recreate anyway, and the run that recreates them is already in the `agents` bundle. Everything else under .claude is taken: settings.json is authored and rides in that bundle, and .claude/worktrees/ is gitignored local scratch that no sync ever sees.
Editor preferences — developer-local, and a consumer's team decides its own.

The bank's inventory of itself. bank:sync reads it out of the fetched bank tree at `ref`, never off the consumer's disk, so vendoring it would put a second, always-staler copy in a repo that already reads the authoritative one.
